question: Your support agent issues refunds through the MCP tool process_refund, whose description reads only "Refunds a customer for an order." Logs show that the agent always picks the right tool, but the backend rejects many of its calls. The agent sends amounts such as "$45.00" while the backend accepts only whole cents such as 4500, and it omits the item ID when a customer returns one item from a multi-item order. Which change most directly reduces these rejected calls?

options.text: Set tool_choice to force process_refund on every turn, so that the agent always reaches the refund tool as soon as a customer mentions a return.
options.reason: Tool selection is already correct, and forced tool selection only controls which tool is called, so it adds no input format or edge case guidance.

options.text: Make the agent retry each rejected process_refund call up to three times with the same arguments before it tells the customer that the refund could not be processed.
options.reason: Repeating the same badly formatted arguments gets the same rejection, because the description still gives no input format and no item ID edge case.

options.text: Expand the process_refund description to state that amounts are whole cents, show an example call, and say that single-item returns need the item ID.
options.reason: The guide says tool descriptions should include input formats, examples and edge cases; this adds the cents format, an example and the single-item return case.

options.text: Rename process_refund to refund_in_cents and keep its one-line description, so that the new tool name alone signals the expected amount format.
options.reason: The guide names the description as the primary mechanism, and a new name keeps the minimal description with no example and no item ID edge case.
